'''''Dactylorhiza maculata''''', known as the '''heath spotted-orchid'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''moorland spotted orchid''', is a [[herbaceous]] [[perennial]] plant of the family [[Orchidaceae]]. It is widespread in mountainous regions across much of Europe from Portugal and Iceland east to Russia. It is also found in Algeria, Morocco, and western Siberia.<ref name="WCSP">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=55410 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=dactylorhiza+maculata Altervista Flora Italiana, Orchide macchiata, Dactylorhiza maculata (L.) Soó ] includes European distribution map</ref> It prefers woods, moorland, bogs, marshes, pastureland and meadows.<ref>[http://www.flowersinsweden.com/Dactylorhizamaculata_page.htm Sweden Flowers: Dactylorhiza ]</ref>

== Etymology ==
The name of the genus ''Dactylorhiza'' is formed from the Greek words δάκτυλος 'daktylos' meaning 'finger' and ρίζα 'ridza' meaning 'root' and refers to the tubers of this plant, which are split into several tubercles. The specific epithet 'maculata', meaning 'spotted', refers to the stained leaves, which is also reflected in the English name "Heath spotted Orchid". The scientific binomial name of this plant was initially ''Orchis maculata'', proposed by the Swedish naturalist and botanist [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753. The name was changed to the one currently accepted (''Dactylorhiza maculata'') by the Hungarian botanist [[Károly Rezső Soó]] in 1962. In German this plant is called {{Lang|de|Geflecktes Knabenkraut}}, in French {{Lang|fr|orchis tacheté}}, and in Italian {{Lang|it|orchide macchiata}} or {{Lang|it|erba d'Adamo}}. In Swedish this plant is called "Virgin Mary's keys".

== Description ==
[[File:Heath spotted-orchid - Flickr - gailhampshire.jpg|thumb|220px|left|Close-up on a flower of ''Dactylorhiza maculata'']] ''Dactylorhiza maculata'' are usually {{convert|15|-|45|cm}} in height, with a maximum of {{convert|70|cm}}. These plants are tuberous geophytes, forming their buds in underground tubers, organs that annually produce new stems, leaves and flowers. Furthermore these orchids are terrestrial: unlike epiphytes they do not live on other large plants.

This orchid has an erect, glabrous and cylindrical stem, with a streaked surface. The leaves are oblong or oval-lanceolate, with dark ellipsoid-shaped spots on the surface (hence the species name). The leaves are [[amplexicaul]] and can be either radical (basal) or cauline.

The underground part of the stem has two tubers, each deeply divided into several lobes or tubercles (characteristic of the genus ''Dactylorhiza'').  The first one has the important function of supplying the stem whilst the second collects nutrients for the development of the plant that will form in the coming year.{{citation needed|date=February 2021}}

The [[inflorescence]] is {{convert|5|-|15|cm}} long and it is composed of flowers gathered in dense spikes. The flowers grow in the axils of bracts membranous and lanceolate-shaped. Their colours vary from light pink to purple or white with darker streaks mainly on the [[Labellum (botany)|labellum]] (sometimes at the margins of [[Tepal|tepals]]). The flowers reach on average {{convert|10|-|15|cm}}. The flowers are [[hermaphrodite]] and insect [[Pollination|pollinated]].

== Habitat ==
The heath spotted orchid prefers sunny places on lowlands or hills.  It can be found in slightly damp meadows but also in the undergrowth of dry forests, in areas with bushes and at the edges of streams. It grows on siliceous and calcareous substrate, at elevations up to {{convert|2200|m}} above sea level. In Northern Europe it flowers in June-July.

== Ecology ==
Orchids in the genus ''Dactylorhiza'' are mycorrhizal generalists. ''D. maculata'' has been found to form associations with a range of common species of [[mycorrhizal fungi]] in the [[Tulasnellaceae]], as well as with species in the [[Ceratobasidiaceae]] and [[Sebacinales]].<ref>{{cite journal | pmc=3411701 | year=2012 | last1=Jacquemyn | first1=H. | last2=Deja | first2=A. | last3=De Hert | first3=K. | last4=Cachapa Bailarote | first4=B. | last5=Lievens | first5=B. | title=Variation in Mycorrhizal Associations with Tulasnelloid Fungi among Populations of Five Dactylorhiza Species | journal=PLOS ONE | volume=7 | issue=8 | article-number=e42212 | doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0042212 | pmid=22870305 | bibcode=2012PLoSO...742212J | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | pmc=5121631 | year=2016 | last1=Jacquemyn | first1=H. | last2=Waud | first2=M. | last3=Merckx | first3=V. S. | last4=Brys | first4=R. | last5=Tyteca | first5=D. | last6=Hedrén | first6=M. | last7=Lievens | first7=B. | title=Habitat-driven variation in mycorrhizal communities in the terrestrial orchid genus Dactylorhiza | journal=Scientific Reports | volume=6 | article-number=37182 | doi=10.1038/srep37182  | doi-access=free| pmid=27883008 | bibcode=2016NatSR...637182J }}</ref>

''Dactylorhiza maculata'' is pollinated by insects, especially [[bumblebees]]. The flowers are 'food deceptive', i.e. do not provide nectar for their pollinators.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1756-1051.2002.tb01621.x | doi=10.1111/j.1756-1051.2002.tb01621.x | title=Pollination and reproductive success of two colour variants of a deceptive orchid, Dactylorhiza maculata (Orchidaceae) | year=2002 | last1=Koivisto | first1=Anna-Maria | last2=Vallius | first2=Elisa | last3=Salonen | first3=Veikko | journal=Nordic Journal of Botany | volume=22 | pages=53–58 | doi-access=free | url-access=subscription }}</ref>
